problem: The lock-up clutch is called 'a plain on/off clutch'. Most production TCUs now apply it with controlled slip (partial lock-up) to smooth torsional vibration, so the flat statement can mislead a student and would lose marks if repeated in an exam.
fix: Say: the lock-up clutch ties the turbine to the impeller to remove converter slip; some TCUs apply it fully on/off, and many apply it with a small controlled slip (partial lock-up) to damp vibration. Either way it does not change the gear ratio; the shift clutches do that.

problem: 'Too early and the engine flares; too late and the car jerks' does not say which event is early or late, so a student cannot tell whether the off-going clutch released too early or the on-coming clutch applied too late.
fix: Write: if the off-going clutch releases too early (before the on-coming clutch carries torque), the engine flares; if it releases too late, both clutches are engaged together and the car jerks (tie-up).

problem: 'If it is longer than target, the TCU lengthens the fill pulse or raises pressure' is stated as a general rule. A long shift caused by low pressure is made worse by a longer fill pulse, and the quiz Q6 answer rightly lengthens the fill pulse only for flare, not for every slow shift. The two statements read as contradictory.
fix: Write: if the shift is slow because the clutch was not yet filled (flare at the start), the TCU lengthens the fill pulse; if the shift is slow because the clutch is slipping under load, it raises pressure. Both are checked against the measured shift time.

problem: The note 'set line pressure' credits all solenoid valves with setting line pressure. Only the pressure control (variable-force) solenoid trims line pressure; the shift solenoids direct oil to the clutch pistons. The figure also shows only the output shaft sensor, while Section 2 uses input shaft speed as well.
fix: Change the note to 'trim line pressure, direct oil to clutches' and add an input shaft speed sensor as a second feedback path into the TCU.

problem: The lead says the TCU reads throttle position, vehicle speed and engine speed, but Q1 asks for the two inputs to the shift map and marks only throttle and vehicle speed. A student may wonder why engine speed is listed and then not accepted.
fix: In the lead, say the TCU reads throttle position, vehicle speed and engine speed, and that the shift map itself is drawn on throttle opening and vehicle speed; engine speed is used for other functions such as slip and ratio monitoring.

problem: The second sentence, 'The gap also lets the schedule favour economy near the boundary', is vague and not explained anywhere in the chapter.
fix: Replace with a clear point: the upshift curve sits at higher speed than the downshift curve, so once an upshift has happened the car must slow noticeably before it drops back, which stops repeated hunting.
